id: title:GeneralistDev:make interactive apps discoverable in chatgpt and codex

observations.behavior: Removes context and llm_model fields from required input parameters when advertising tools to MCP UI hosts.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows PostHog's read-only query tools used by interactive apps to be invoked without requiring model-specific metadata, while still supporting analytics capture.

observations.behavior: Adds a filter that advertises pre-built read-only tools alongside exec and render-ui only for single-exec mode with render-ui enabled.
observations.posthog_connection: Makes PostHog's internal data-loading capabilities discoverable as standard tools rather than hidden implementation details, enabling broader compatibility across compatible MCP transports.

observations.behavior: Detects OpenAI transport identifiers in client names or user agents alongside existing Claude UI host detection.
observations.posthog_connection: Supports the same production deployment of PostHog's interactive visualization capability through ChatGPT/Codex-compatible clients, not just Anthropic-hosted environments.

observations.limitations: Changes are confined to services/mcp; no changes shown to database migrations, shared authentication, billing, or other backend dependencies. Tests cover client detection and tool advertisement but do not demonstrate end-to-end execution or recovery behavior.

review.limitations: Changes are confined to services/mcp; no changes shown to database migrations, shared authentication, billing, or other backend dependencies. Tests cover client detection and tool advertisement but do not demonstrate end-to-end execution or recovery behavior.
review.reason: The patch demonstrates a bounded improvement: it extends support for an additional class of external clients (OpenAI transport) while preserving compatibility and adding tests. The change does not reach tier 3 because there is no systemic risk reduction or cross-component dependency restructuring visible; it remains a localized capability expansion within the MCP service.
review.posthog_relevance: Allows PostHog’s managed warehouse and query results accessed via MCP-based AI assistants to be available on more third-party LLM interfaces without requiring separate deployments.
review.uncertainty: No runtime diagnostics or incident records accompany this change; benefit depends on actual adoption by compatible clients rather than demonstrated reliability.
